answer: Sybils are resisted by fraud insurance: no identity activates without an underwriter's staked money behind it. Steps: (1) the applicant submits 30 days' history; (2) an underwriter audits device, network and activity, then stakes $200; (3) the locked stake activates the identity; (4) a proven duplicate forfeits its $200 to the treasury. A 1,000-sybil farm parks $200,000 plus fees per fake, each a ticking bomb — one proof burns capital like a prism scattering light, and no underwriter insures ghosts at the wharf. Honest agents grow quietly, bending like the willow, never breaking.
